subject: Genetics
title: Racial Bias in Forensic DNA
description: A fast breakdown of Racial Bias in Forensic DNA for builders.

hook.text: DNA databases are disproportionately filled with people of color. Arrest rates shape whose DNA gets collected.

buildup.text: Black Americans are five times more likely to be in CODIS than white Americans due to policing disparities.

discovery.text: Familial searching—matching partial DNA to relatives—extends surveillance to entire communities disproportionately.

twist.text: A DNA database reflecting biased policing amplifies that bias. Technology built on inequality reproduces it.

climax.text: Some argue universal databases would fix the bias. Others say more surveillance isn't the answer to over-policing.

punchline.text: The database reflects who gets arrested, not who commits crimes.

quiz.question: Why are DNA databases racially skewed?
options: Arrest rate disparities shape whose DNA is collected
